n9bed96357f.headline: Bitcoin Price Rose to $5,900 after Fed Zero-Rate Cut but Then Fell Below $5,000
n9bed96357f.summary: Bitcoin briefly climbed to $5,900 after the US Federal Reserve announced a large rate cut, before falling back below $5,000. The move highlights volatility in crypto markets.
n9bed96357f.why: Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency, and its price often reacts to changes in US interest rates and broader risk sentiment.

impacts.name: Bitcoin
impacts.why: Bitcoin rose on news of the Fed cut but then fell back below $5,000.

n9bed96357f.why_moved: Bitcoin initially gained on the US Federal Reserve's large rate cut, but the gain did not hold and the price dropped back below $5,000.

nb42a5aad01.headline: Recession fears spur tumble for Thai equities
nb42a5aad01.summary: Thailand's stock exchange fell at the start of the week as recession fears and rising local coronavirus cases outweighed the US Federal Reserve's rate cut and quantitative easing.
nb42a5aad01.why: The Stock Exchange of Thailand is the main equity market for Thai listed companies, which are sensitive to tourism and export demand.
nb42a5aad01.why_moved: Recession fears and rising local coronavirus cases outweighed the effect of the US Federal Reserve's rate cut and quantitative easing.

nc26ee26eb7.headline: Oil prices extend losses on price war, virus fallout
nc26ee26eb7.summary: Oil prices fell further on Monday after a Saudi-Russian price war and an equities sell-off sparked by the coronavirus pandemic produced their biggest weekly losses in over a decade.
nc26ee26eb7.why: Brent crude is the global benchmark for oil prices, and producer decisions and demand shocks directly affect energy companies, transport costs and inflation expectations.
nc26ee26eb7.why_moved: A Saudi-Russian price war combined with an equities sell-off tied to the coronavirus pandemic drove the losses.

n9f4603429e.headline: Coronavirus Pandemic Forces the Fed to Unleash a Massive Bazooka – Welcome to the Era of Zero/Negative Interest Rates
n9f4603429e.summary: The Federal Reserve has unleashed a large round of stimulus to dampen the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on the US economy. The move points toward near-zero or negative interest rates.
n9f4603429e.why: The Federal Reserve sets US interest rates and monetary policy, which affects borrowing costs, bond yields and asset valuations worldwide.
n9f4603429e.why_moved: The Fed announced a large stimulus package in response to the coronavirus pandemic, signalling a move toward near-zero or negative rates.

n280c923d38.headline: Australian government announces $17.5bn stimulus package
n280c923d38.summary: The Australian federal government unveiled a AUD 17.5 billion stimulus package to support the economy during the coronavirus pandemic.
n280c923d38.why: Fiscal stimulus aims to boost economic activity and mitigate recession risks during the pandemic-induced downturn.
